parts.gloss: hiding behind the guise of penance

words.gloss: hiding behind the guise of penance

literal: Hiding behind penance, doing evil deeds, is like a hunter hiding behind a bush and trapping birds.
translation: Performing evil deeds while hiding behind the guise of penance is like a hunter hiding behind a bush to trap birds.
modern: தவ வேடத்திற்குப் பின்னால் மறைந்து கொண்டு தீய செயல்களைச் செய்வது, ஒரு வேடன் புதருக்குப் பின்னால் மறைந்து பறவைகளைப் பிடிப்பதற்கு ஒப்பானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid simile to expose the hypocrisy of those who pretend to be ascetics while committing sins. The poet compares a false ascetic to a hunter. Just as a hunter hides behind a bush (புதல்) to deceive and trap unsuspecting birds (புள்), a hypocrite uses the outward appearance of penance (தவம்) as a shield to perform evil deeds (அல்லவை) without being suspected. The key words 'தவமறைந்து' (hiding behind penance) and 'புதல்மறைந்து' (hiding behind a bush) draw a direct parallel between religious hypocrisy and predatory deception.
